results: 1. Directly observe gait barefoot at normal, fast, slow, tandem, backward, sideways, and while performing a dual task.
tandem gait: better than free walking
walking backward: the scissoring DISAPPEARS on walking backward; in spasticity it persists
gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards): the pattern changes or normalises
observation for excessive slowness or uneconomic posture: not present
2. Perform a complete neurological examination, including tone, power, reflexes, plantar responses, sensation, coordination, and cranial nerves.
cranial nerve examination: normal
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal reflexes, FLEXOR plantar responses, no clonus
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): normal tone on passive movement despite the scissoring gait
cerebellar examination (finger-nose, dysdiadochokinesis, nystagmus): normal
MRC power in all four limbs: 5/5 throughout
3. Test for inconsistency with repeated hip abduction, straight-leg raising, and lower-limb resistance manoeuvres.
Hoover sign / hip-abductor sign: negative
4. Perform a pull test and assess postural stability.
posture and pull test: normal
5. Obtain brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging.
MRI brain: normal, no periventricular lesions
MRI diffusion-weighted sequences: normal
6. Obtain cervical and thoracic spinal MRI.
MRI cervical and thoracic spine: normal cord, no compression, no signal change
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder with functional gait disturbance (incongruent, distractible scissoring gait), without evidence of structural neurological disease.

Alternative: Task-specific functional dystonia of the lower limbs.

Alternative: Organic task-specific gait dystonia.

Alternative: Factitious or feigned gait disorder.
